min_demand_threshold.detail: Rule applies to large load customers with total expected non-coincident peak demand of 75 MW or more at a single site.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: An entity requesting a new or expanded interconnection where the customer’s total expected non-coincident peak demand at a single site is equal to or exceeds 75 MW

collateral.detail: Financial security of $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand (or incremental increase) must be posted with the intermediate agreement; further security is posted at SLLIA execution; unused security is returned or forfeited under set conditions.
collateral.verbatim: must post financial security with the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP in the amount of $50,000 per MW of the requested peak demand for new interconnection requests

study_requirements.detail: Customers pay a $100,000 study fee before the request is included in an interconnection study; unused study amounts are returned within 60 days.
study_requirements.verbatim: A large load customer must pay a study fee of $100,000 to the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP for transmission studies

direct_cost_assignment.detail: Customers pay direct interconnection costs through cash CIAC with no allowance offsetting it.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: A large load customer must pay all direct interconnection costs through CIAC, with no standard or other allowance offered to offset the customer’s CIAC payments.

dca_interconnection.detail: Direct interconnection costs (significant equipment and services) are paid as non-refundable CIAC in cash.
dca_interconnection.verbatim: CIAC must be paid in the form of a direct cash payment.

min_billing_demand.detail: The standard large load interconnection agreement must acknowledge that the customer will pay the large load minimum billing demand set in 16 TAC 25.193; the percentage is in that separate rule.
min_billing_demand.verbatim: The SLLIA must include a term of acknowledgment and agreement that the large load customer will pay the large load minimum billing demand described in §25.193

load_forecast_requirement.detail: Customers must disclose a month-and-year schedule for phased energization of requested peak demand and give progress updates when requested; no periodic forecast cadence is set.
load_forecast_requirement.verbatim: A large load customer must provide updates or progress reports to the interconnecting DSP or the interconnecting TSP when requested.

customer_resource_procurement.detail: Statute directs standards on load curtailment and on-site backup generation deployment during emergencies.
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: require the large load customer to either deploy the customer's on-site backup generating facilities or curtail load.

load_flexibility.detail: SB 6 allows ERCOT to direct large loads (75 MW+) to curtail or deploy on-site backup generation in emergencies and requires a competitive demand-reduction procurement program.
load_flexibility.verbatim: requires each large load to remain curtailed for the duration of the energy emergency alert event or until the load can be recalled safely

status_note: Final rule 16 TAC 25.194 adopted by PUCT in Project 58481 (adoption order text read; dated 2026 per Texas Register proposal of March 27, 2026; approx. Sept 2026). The old seed said $50,000/MW non-refundable interconnection fee; the adopted rule has $100,000 study fee + $50,000/MW refundable-in-conditions security, with cash CIAC for direct costs. Docket: Project No. 58481.

customer_resource_procurement.detail: Proposed ISA amendment would let a co-located load take supply from the adjacent Susquehanna generation behind the point of interconnection; the amendment was rejected.
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: to increase the amount of Co-Located Load from 300 megawatts (MW) to 480 MW and to make revisions related to the treatment of this Co-Located Load

btm_generation.detail: Co-located load of up to 480 MW (up from 300 MW) on the generator side of the interconnection point; FERC rejected the non-conforming amendment on Nov 1, 2024.
btm_generation.verbatim: we find that PJM has not demonstrated that the proposed non-conforming provisions in the Amended ISA are necessary deviations from the pro forma ISA

status_note: Rejected by FERC 2024-11-01 (order text read). Federal interconnection service agreement, not a retail rate design, so almost no LBL elements apply; entries describe the rejected proposal only.

min_demand_threshold.detail: Model tariff applies at 50 MW individually; utility may apply it below the threshold case by case.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: This tariff is applicable to customers at or over 50 MW individually or 100 MW in the aggregate.

aggregation_rules.detail: 100 MW threshold applies to multiple closely located customers in aggregate; behind-the-meter generation is excluded from the threshold calculation.
aggregation_rules.verbatim: multiple closely located customers with maximum Contract Capacity of 100 MW in the aggregate

min_contract_duration.detail: Initial Contract Term of at least five years, starting after the load ramp period; company may require longer to recover its investment.
min_contract_duration.verbatim: A Large Load Customer’s Initial Contract Term should be made for a period of not less than five (5) years.

monthly_demand_charge.detail: Customers may be charged higher monthly demand charges than the minimum so the utility fully recovers fixed costs; rates are set in each utility's own tariff.
monthly_demand_charge.verbatim: Large Load Customers may be subject to higher monthly demand changes to allow the utility to fully recover fixed costs associated with serving the Large Load Customers’ load.

min_billing_demand.detail: Monthly billing demand is no less than the greater of 80% of contract capacity or 80% of the highest billing demand in the prior 11 months.
min_billing_demand.verbatim: Eighty (80) percent of the Large Load Customer's contract capacity specified for the applicable period of the Contract Term

min_bill.detail: Minimum monthly demand charge equal to 80% of contracted demand; customer pays minimum charges during the initial term even if it curtails, suspends or terminates.
min_bill.verbatim: Large Load Customers will be subject to a minimum monthly demand charge equal to 80% of the contracted demand.

collateral.detail: Collateral must fully cover Network Improvement and Interconnection Facilities costs, in cash, letter of credit or A-/A3-rated parent guarantee, and is reduced as milestones are met.
collateral.verbatim: Collateral requirements should be provided in sufficient amounts to fully cover Network Improvement Costs and Interconnection Facilities costs.

direct_cost_assignment.detail: Customer pays interconnection facilities and network improvement costs through CIAC on a 'but for' basis.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: The Company will assess CIAC for Large Load Customer additions to recover all distribution and transmission costs necessary to interconnect the new Large Load Customer.

dca_interconnection.detail: Interconnection Facilities that solely benefit the customer are assigned to it through CIAC.
dca_interconnection.verbatim: Large Load Customers are subject to a fee for Interconnection Facilities costs and Network Improvement Costs through CIAC.

dca_network_transmission.detail: Network Improvement costs, including transmission, are allocated to the customer when they would not be needed but for its interconnection, even if others benefit.
dca_network_transmission.verbatim: If a Network Improvement would not have been needed “but for” the interconnection of the Large Load Customer, then the costs of the upgrade will be allocated to that customer

customer_resource_procurement.detail: Model tariff includes interruptible service and onsite-generation options.
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: Large Load Customers bringing their own onsite generation and not using their full interconnection service request may be offered lower minimum demand charges and/or standby charges

btm_generation.detail: Customers with onsite generation may be offered lower minimum demand or standby charges at utility discretion; onsite generation offsetting grid demand in a curtailment counts as curtailment.
btm_generation.verbatim: A Large Load Customer bringing onsite generation and using that generation to offset demand for the Large Load Customer’s grid services during a curtailment event will be treated as having curtailed.

load_flexibility.detail: Interruptible service contracts with mandatory capacity interruptions, penalties for failure to curtail, and removal to firm rate if the customer does not curtail.
load_flexibility.verbatim: Contract Service for Interruptible Power will be available to Large Load Customer customers based on the Company’s existing interruptible service tariff provisions.

price_premium.detail: Annual universal service program contribution scaled by peak demand, from $250,000 (25-75 MW) to $1,000,000 (500 MW or more).
price_premium.verbatim: Large Load Customers are to make an annual contribution to the Company’s universal service program based on the following peak demand schedule

study_requirements.detail: Customer pays full planning study costs; twice-yearly cluster 'Network Open Season'; studies due within six months or 50% of fee is refunded per 90-day delay.
study_requirements.verbatim: Interconnection Studies will be completed within six (6) months from the date that an application for interconnection study is accepted by the Company as complete.

load_ramp_period.detail: Customer may designate a load ramp period of 3 to 5 years; the initial contract term starts after it ends.
load_ramp_period.verbatim: A Customer may designate a Load Ramp Period, which should be at or between three (3) years and five (5) years.

resize_reassign.detail: After five years customers may cut capacity by up to 20% without fee on 48 months notice; utility will try to reassign released capacity to other large loads.
resize_reassign.verbatim: the Company will use reasonable efforts, consistent with its obligations as a public utility, to mitigate the Exit Fee amount owed or paid by the Large Load Customer

exit_fee.detail: Exit fee is the greater of unrecovered network/interconnection costs or the remaining minimum charge on the reduced capacity, over an Exit Fee Period of 1 to 5 years; 48 months notice.
exit_fee.verbatim: The Exit Fee will be calculated as the greater of (1) the difference between the cost of Network Improvements and Interconnection Facilities less the revenues received from the Large Load Customer

status_note: Final Order adopted April 30, 2026, entered May 12, 2026 at M-2025-3054271 (approved confirmed from the order text). Model tariff is guidance for each EDC to file, not a tariff in force.

min_demand_threshold.detail: Large load customer agreement required at 20 MW; Schedule 96 applies to data centers of 20 MW or more under HB 3546.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: Revise Rule I to lower minimum threshold for customers that require an LLCA to 20 MW.

customer_type.detail: Schedule 96 is a class for data centers (NAICS 518210) of 20 MW or more, set up under Oregon HB 3546.
customer_type.verbatim: a facility that uses or is able to use 20 megawatts or more and is primarily engaged in providing a service described under the 2022 North American Industry Classification System Code 518210

min_contract_duration.detail: 10 years at 20 MW, rising 1 year per 10 MW to 30 years at 220 MW or more.
min_contract_duration.verbatim: require a term of 10 years for a 20 MW load, with the term increasing by one year for each 10 MW increment in load up to a maximum of 30 years for a load 220 MW or greater

monthly_demand_charge.detail: Schedule 96 has transmission and related service, distribution, system usage and generation demand charges, at primary and subtransmission service levels.
monthly_demand_charge.verbatim: basic charge, transmission and related service charge, distribution charges, system usage charge, and generation demand charge

min_billing_demand.detail: Minimum generation demand and minimum transmission demand set at 90% of contracted capacity.
min_billing_demand.verbatim: We adopt a MGD and MTD of90 percent

collateral.detail: Uniform credit requirements in the tariff (A- S&P / A3 Moody's debt rating), surety bonds allowed; plus a capacity allocation deposit of two years of minimum transmission demand, refundable 50% in year 2 and 50% in year 3 post-energization.
collateral.verbatim: charging a system capacity allocation deposit due at contract signing equal to two years of minimum transmission demand

direct_cost_assignment.detail: Transmission built to serve one customer is directly assigned to it; non-permanent transmission upgrades are 100% allocated to the benefiting customer; customers may pay CIAC up to 100% of distribution assets.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: when a transmission asset is built to serve a single customer, it is appropriate to directly assign the costs of that transmission asset to that customer

dca_interconnection.detail: Customers with an LLCA or MLA can contribute up to 100% CIAC for non-shared distribution assets; 100% of non-permanent transmission upgrade costs go to the beneficiary.
dca_interconnection.verbatim: We find it appropriate to allocate 100 percent of the costs for any nonpermanent transmission facility upgrades to the customer benefiting from the nonpermanent upgrade.

dca_network_transmission.detail: Single-customer transmission is directly assigned; customers 20 MW and above may fund CIAC up to 100% of generation and transmission investments.
dca_network_transmission.verbatim: The record shows that direct assignment paired with the PGM can fairly allocate transmission costs.

dca_generation_capacity.detail: Customers 20 MW+ may pay CIAC up to 100% of generation and transmission investment; growth-related generation is allocated by the PGM to growth classes.
dca_generation_capacity.verbatim: generation investments will be considered growth-related when they are triggered by the need for incremental capacity or energy to reliably serve increased demand

customer_resource_procurement.detail: Special contracts for dedicated resources are considered case by case; direct access allowed with transition charges.
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: We will consider special contracts on a case-by-case.

customer_led_procurement.detail: Customers can contract directly with PGE for dedicated resources via special contracts with a list of permissible resources; direct access also allowed with safeguards.
customer_led_procurement.verbatim: We accept the Coalition's proposed list of permissible resources for special contracts.

load_flexibility.detail: No flexible-load subclass or fast-track queue; flexibility is recognized as a credit in special contracts and as one element of a plan of service.
load_flexibility.verbatim: we decline to create a subclass for flexible loads

price_premium.detail: 1 cent/kWh surcharge on Schedule 96 customers with allocated capacity of 100 MW or more, plus the maximum HB 3141 public-purpose contribution from all Schedule 96 customers.
price_premium.verbatim: We find that applying a surcharge of 1 cent per kWh to Schedule 96 customers with an Allocated System Capacity of 100 MW or greater

study_requirements.detail: Study costs are customer-paid; PGE gets a flat study fee for loads under 4 MW and study results expire after 60 days unless extended.
study_requirements.verbatim: charge a flat fee for all studies for customers under 4 MW

hold_harmless.detail: Cost allocation uses a Planned Growth Method (PGM) that assigns growth-related generation and transmission costs to the classes driving growth, indefinitely.
hold_harmless.verbatim: We find the PGM will fairly allocate costs of growth to the classes of customers responsible for that growth and thus will prevent cost shifting

formulaic_backstop.detail: An 'EGM' mechanism was found generally reasonable for mitigating cost shift under the POWER Act; exit-fee revenue is applied to the departing class's revenue requirement.
formulaic_backstop.verbatim: We find PGE's proposal for an EGM to be generally reasonable and consistent with the POWER Act's requirement

marginal_cost.detail: Order updates PGE's marginal cost studies, including separate substation marginal costs by class, and adopts the PGM for growth-related cost allocation.
marginal_cost.verbatim: calculate separate substation marginal costs by class to account for the significant differences in the way various customer classes use distribution infrastructure

resize_reassign.detail: Exit fee may be refunded in whole or part, prorated, when another customer takes the exiting customer's capacity within three years.
resize_reassign.verbatim: to allow refunds of the exit fee in whole or in part when another customer assumes the exiting customer's capacity within three years

exit_fee.detail: Exit fees apply to distribution costs below 20 MW and are extended to transmission and generation costs for loads of 20 MW and above; revenue goes to the departing customer's class.
exit_fee.verbatim: we find the Coalition's proposed exit fee for transmission and generation costs should be added for loads 20 MW and greater

status_note: Order No. 26-154 entered 2026-05-07 adopts Schedule 96 with modifications (approved confirmed from order text). Also creates an interconnection queue requiring a reliable HB 2021-compliant plan of service before energization.

lbl_appendix_name: Xcel Energy Colorado — Large General Service – Transmission (26AL-0137E)

min_demand_threshold.detail: Proposed tariff applies to new customers or expansions of 50 MW or more; customers of 20-50 MW may also be subject to it.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: this tariff would apply to new customers or significant expansion of existing electric load of 50 megawatts (MW) or more.

min_contract_duration.detail: Proposed long-term commitments of typically 15 years or more.
min_contract_duration.verbatim: Large customers must make long-term contractual commitments — typically 15 years or more.

min_bill.detail: Proposed minimum monthly payment toward infrastructure built to serve the customer, even while load ramps up; no percentage stated in the release.
min_bill.verbatim: Large customers contribute toward the cost of infrastructure constructed and available to serve them, even if load ramps up gradually.

collateral.detail: Proposed financial security requirements for projects that are delayed, scaled back or not completed; amount not stated in the release.
collateral.verbatim: Financial security requirements add extra protection if a project is delayed, scaled back or not completed.

direct_cost_assignment.detail: Large customers would pay for the transmission, substations, interconnection upgrades and new generation needed to serve them.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: large customers would pay for the power infrastructure needed to serve them.

dca_interconnection.detail: Customers cover interconnection upgrades and substations.
dca_interconnection.verbatim: This includes covering electric transmission, substations and interconnection upgrades as well as paying for new electric generation.

dca_network_transmission.detail: Customers cover electric transmission needed to serve them.
dca_network_transmission.verbatim: This includes covering electric transmission, substations and interconnection upgrades as well as paying for new electric generation.

dca_generation_capacity.detail: Customers pay for new electric generation procured to serve them.
dca_generation_capacity.verbatim: as well as paying for new electric generation

exit_fee.detail: Termination charges recover remaining costs of project-specific upgrades if a customer exits early.
exit_fee.verbatim: termination charges will recover remaining costs of project-specific upgrades built, avoiding stranded costs for other customers.

hold_harmless.detail: Stated aim that existing customers do not subsidize large new customers; the release gives no revenue-versus-cost test (LBL describes Xcel's Schedule TL test separately).
hold_harmless.verbatim: This ensures that existing customers are not paying for the needs of the large load customers.

status_note: Still proposed: Colorado PUC suspended the tariff's effective date to Jan 8, 2027 (Decision C26-0467, mailed 2026-07-10; 26AL-0137E); hearings scheduled Aug 25 and Oct 20, 2026. Only the company's release was read for element detail; the filed Schedule TL text was not reachable. Search reports mention 24-month exit notice and an 80% minimum bill but only from secondary sources, so not stored.

direct_cost_assignment.detail: Proposal splits project-specific infrastructure into a Customer Contributed Share paid by the large-load customer and a System Benefit Share that can be reviewed for rate base.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: The proposal splits project-specific infrastructure into a Customer Contributed Share, paid by the large-load customer, and a System Benefit Share

dca_interconnection.detail: NV Energy would track substations and transmission facilities needed to serve the customer on a customer-specific asset schedule, paid by upfront contribution or ongoing facility payments.
dca_interconnection.verbatim: Large-load customers would pay for the project-specific share of those investments, either through an upfront contribution or ongoing facility payments.

dca_generation_capacity.detail: Customer-specific asset schedule covers generation facilities needed to serve the customer; customers may directly fund or finance new generation.
dca_generation_capacity.verbatim: NV Energy would identify and track substations, generation and transmission facilities needed to serve a large-load customer on a customer-specific asset schedule.

dca_network_transmission.detail: Transmission facilities needed to serve the customer are tracked and charged to it, with customers able to fund or finance new transmission.
dca_network_transmission.verbatim: allowing tech companies to directly fund or finance new generation and transmission infrastructure needed to serve their demand

exit_fee.detail: Final exit charge if the customer leaves before infrastructure payments are complete; amount not specified in the article.
exit_fee.verbatim: with a final exit charge if they leave before those payments are complete

load_ramp_period.detail: Electric service agreement would set a defined contract demand and load ramp; no ramp length given.
load_ramp_period.verbatim: Customers would enter into an electric service agreement with a defined contract demand and load ramp.

customer_resource_procurement.detail: Bring Your Own Power provision lets customers procure third-party generation.
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: A “Bring Your Own Power” provision allows customers to procure generation from third-party providers

customer_led_procurement.detail: Third-party generation procured by the customer has accredited capacity incorporated into utility planning assumptions.
customer_led_procurement.verbatim: with accredited capacity incorporated into utility planning assumptions

status_note: Still proposed: filed May 2026 at PUCN; no decision as of the June 8, 2026 article. Secondary reporting says public comment through Oct 2026, hearings Jan 2027, decision mid-2027 (not stored). The filed tariff itself was not reachable; details are from Utility Dive (DCD returned 403).

lbl_appendix_name: Commonwealth Edison — Revisions to General Terms & Conditions for Large Loads (25-0677)

min_demand_threshold.detail: Applies to projects whose projected load ramp reaches 50 MW or more of Maximum Kilowatts Delivered within ten calendar years of requested service.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: equal to or greater than 50 MW at any time before December of the tenth (10th) calendar year after the requested date of service

collateral.detail: Deposit of $1,000,000 plus $500,000 per additional whole 100 MW above 200 MW; amount over $2,000,000 must be backed by an Acceptable Letter of Credit; refunded when service starts.
collateral.verbatim: the sum of $1,000,000 plus $500,000 for each additional whole 100 MW of MKD above 200 MW

study_requirements.detail: Customers provide security for ComEd's analysis and engineering costs; ComEd may combine requests into a Cluster Study of transmission and distribution impacts.
study_requirements.verbatim: A Large Demand Project Applicant or Customer is required to provide a security for the Company’s analysis and engineering costs.

min_contract_duration.detail: No retail contract term; a Transmission Security Agreement guarantees transmission payments for 10 years after service begins.
min_contract_duration.verbatim: will not for a period of ten (10) years after the commencement of service fall below the annual payment that would be made by a customer meeting the load ramp submitted to ComEd

min_bill.detail: Annual transmission service payments are guaranteed at no less than the amount a customer meeting its submitted load ramp would pay, for 10 years.
min_bill.verbatim: guarantee that its annual payments for transmission service, calculated in accordance with Attachment H-13 of the PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT)

load_ramp_period.detail: Applicant submits a projected monthly load ramp, used to size the deposit and the transmission guarantee; no maximum ramp length set.
load_ramp_period.verbatim: “load ramp” and “projected load ramp” both mean the anticipated monthly request of new or increased electrical usage in MW

explicit_load_forecast.detail: Applicants must provide a projected monthly load ramp with the application.
explicit_load_forecast.verbatim: a deposit calculated based on the MKD included in the load ramp provided by the Application or Customer

load_forecast_requirement.detail: Applicants must provide a projected monthly load ramp with the application.
load_forecast_requirement.verbatim: a deposit calculated based on the MKD included in the load ramp provided by the Application or Customer

hold_harmless.detail: Transmission revenue shortfalls from a large load are recovered from it under the TSA and credited to other transmission customers in the ComEd zone.
hold_harmless.verbatim: If there is a revenue shortfall from the LDPAC in any year, the delta will be recovered under the TSA with that LDPAC

formulaic_backstop.detail: Annual shortfall between guaranteed and actual transmission payments is collected and credited to the transmission revenue requirement of other customers.
formulaic_backstop.verbatim: credited to the transmission revenue requirement borne by transmission customers in the ComEd zone

status_note: Approved: ICC order of March 19, 2026 in consolidated Dockets 25-0677/25-0679; compliance tariff sheets filed March 30, effective March 31, 2026 (read from the compliance filing). Order itself blocked by ICC bot wall; ICC opened follow-on proceedings per Capitol News Illinois.

lbl_appendix_name: Arizona Public Service — Extra High Load Factor (E-01345A-25-0105)

customer_type.detail: The Extra High Load Factor rate applies to large load users such as manufacturers and data centers; APS proposed updating its eligibility.
customer_type.verbatim: Extra High Load Factor (which applies to large load users, such as manufacturing companies and data centers)

min_contract_duration.detail: APS says data center customers would sign long-term contracts covering infrastructure costs; no term length stated in the sources read.
min_contract_duration.verbatim: Data center customers would sign long-term contracts covering the costs to build and maintain infrastructure over the long-term

direct_cost_assignment.detail: APS proposes future infrastructure needs be paid for by the data center customers who would use it.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: future infrastructure needs are paid for by the data center customers who would use it, not by existing residential or business customers

customer_resource_procurement.detail: APS proposed a bring-your-own-power policy to workshop participants at the ACC.
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: a bring your own power policy that would directly assign the costs to produce new electricity generation

customer_led_procurement.detail: Proposed bring-your-own-power policy directly assigns the cost of new generation to the customer.
customer_led_procurement.verbatim: a bring your own power policy that would directly assign the costs to produce new electricity generation

dca_generation_capacity.detail: Proposed policy assigns the cost of new generation to the data center customer.
dca_generation_capacity.verbatim: a bring your own power policy that would directly assign the costs to produce new electricity generation

hold_harmless.detail: Proposed formula rates test annually whether rates recover cost to serve each class and adjust them so residential customers do not bear data center growth costs.
hold_harmless.verbatim: This annual process would verify that residential and other business customers are not receiving cost increases associated with data center growth.

formulaic_backstop.detail: Formula Rate Adjustment Mechanism proposed: APS checks cost to serve each year and assigns increases caused by extra-large customers to them.
formulaic_backstop.verbatim: If extra-large customers like data centers cause costs to rise, those costs will be assigned to them.

price_premium.detail: APS proposed a rate increase of more than 45% for extra-large users so they cover their cost of service.
price_premium.verbatim: we proposed a 45% rate increase for these extra-large energy users

status_note: Still pending: hearing ran May 18 to July 7, 2026; ALJ Recommended Opinion and Order expected late November 2026; Commission vote deadline Dec 31, 2026; new rates early 2027 (ACC, July 10, 2026). Tariff text (thresholds, minimum demand, load factor) not found; elements come from APS and ACC web pages. LBL notes APS proposed removing the 92% minimum load factor.

lbl_appendix_name: Duke Energy Carolinas — Schedule HLF (High Load Factor) (E-7 Sub 1329)

min_demand_threshold.detail: Applies at 50 MW contract demand with 80% expected load factor, or at 150 MW contract demand at any load factor, for agreements executed on or after June 1, 2026.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: a total contract demand of 50 MW or more and an expected 12-month rolling average load factor of 80% of more, or (b) a total contract demand of 150 MW or more and any load factor

aggregation_rules.detail: Customers at one premises or multiple premises within one mile of each other are treated together.
aggregation_rules.verbatim: served at either a single premises, or at multiple premises within one mile of each other

load_factor_threshold.detail: Expected 12-month rolling average load factor of 80% or more for the 50 MW tier; measured on forecast at full operation, with move-in if actual use later meets it.
load_factor_threshold.verbatim: expected load factor shall be determined using the customer’s forecasted twelve (12) month rolling average at full operation

min_contract_duration.detail: Below 100 MW: greater of 10 years or 5 years plus load ramp; 100 MW or more: greater of 15 years or 10 years plus load ramp; then one-year auto-extensions with 24 months notice.
min_contract_duration.verbatim: The minimum initial contract term for ESAs of 100 MW or more will be the greater of (a) 15 years and (b) 10 years plus the load ramp period.

monthly_demand_charge.detail: Customers are served under Schedule HLF, whose demand charges are subject to a 75% billing demand floor.
monthly_demand_charge.verbatim: Billing demand will not be less than 75% of contract demand for all demand charges in Schedule HLF.

min_billing_demand.detail: Billing demand at least 75% of contract demand for all HLF demand charges, from when contract demand takes effect.
min_billing_demand.verbatim: Billing demand will not be less than 75% of contract demand for all demand charges in Schedule HLF.

collateral.detail: Security equal to early-termination liquidated damages in cash, letter of credit or parent guarantee; separate letter of credit for the cost of transmission network upgrades.
collateral.verbatim: The customer must provide security equal to the applicable liquidated damages for early termination in the form of cash, letter of credit or parent guarantee

direct_cost_assignment.detail: Dedicated facilities funded in advance as CIAC; transmission network upgrades secured by letter of credit, with a direct-assignment methodology due within 12 months of approval.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: The customer will provide advanced funds equal to the estimated total cost of Dedicated Facilities as a contribution in aid of construction (CIAC)

dca_interconnection.detail: Customer pays estimated dedicated facilities cost as CIAC within 60 days of the letter agreement and covers actual overruns.
dca_interconnection.verbatim: The customer will further provide all necessary additional funds to cover the actual cost of such Dedicated Facilities

dca_network_transmission.detail: Customer posts a letter of credit for estimated network upgrade costs; any portion later direct-assigned by an approved method is paid as CIAC.
dca_network_transmission.verbatim: The customer will provide a deposit in the form of a letter of credit equal to the estimated total cost of transmission network upgrades necessary to serve the customer load

customer_resource_procurement.detail: Reliability provision lets an ESA use alternative Commission-approved options that accelerate capacity resources; no customer-led procurement program.
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: Alternative Commission-approved options that accelerate capacity resources on the utility system during the integration of the customer’s full contract demand

load_flexibility.detail: Each ESA includes interruptibility of 95% of load for up to 50 hours/year or 50% for up to 100 hours/year during the ramp period plus one year; uncompensated.
load_flexibility.verbatim: Interruptibility of 95% of contract load for up to 50 hours per year for the load ramp period plus one year of service

load_ramp_period.detail: Contract term is the greater of a fixed term or a shorter fixed term plus the load ramp period; no maximum ramp length set in the tariff.
load_ramp_period.verbatim: The minimum initial contract term for ESAs below 100 MW will be the greater of (a) 10 years and (b) 5 years plus the load ramp period.

exit_fee.detail: Liquidated damages: 100% of minimum billing demand charges during notice period, NPV of remaining extra facilities charges, plus 25% of remaining minimum billing demand charges.
exit_fee.verbatim: plus (3) 25% of remaining minimum billing demand charges at the customer’s annual contract demand under the remaining term of the contract

resize_reassign.detail: After the 6th anniversary a customer may cut contract demand once by up to 20% (max 200 MW) without liquidated damages; notice of 24 to 48 months otherwise.
resize_reassign.verbatim: the customer may provide notice to reduce contract demand by up to 20% but no greater than 200 MW, one time, without incurring liquidated damages

status_note: Large Load Tariff settlement filed Oct 6, 2026 (Docket E-7 Sub 1329 / E-2 Sub 1380; Duke, Public Staff, Amazon, Google, Microsoft and others) for effect Jan 1, 2027; NCUC has not approved it as of the stipulation text read, so still proposed. Supersedes the July 2026 settlement note (that one only committed to a separate LLT proceeding). Applies to both DEC and DEP.

customer_type.detail: Tax applies to data center operators; 'data center' is defined by primary use, excluding facilities whose primary function is internet access or communication service.
customer_type.verbatim: “Data center” does not include a facility whose primary function is to facilitate the provision of internet access service, a communication service as defined in § 58.1-647

min_demand_threshold.detail: Definition of data center requires electrical equipment managing at least one megawatt of capacity; no other size floor.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: equipment used for the transformation, transmission, distribution, or management of at least one megawatt of capacity of electrical power and cooling

price_premium.detail: Tax of $0.011/kWh on all data center electricity consumed, July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2028; general fund receives up to $600M/yr, excess is refunded pro rata to operators. It is a state tax, not a utility rate.
price_premium.verbatim: an electricity consumption tax at the rate of $0.011/kWh of all electricity consumed at each data center per month

status_note: Enacted: budget signed by Gov. Spanberger June 30, 2026, tax in effect July 1, 2026, sunsets July 1, 2028 (per BDO/WhiteFord/techtimes results from one search; statute text read at the LIS conference-report amendment). This is a state tax, not a utility tariff, so nearly all LBL elements do not apply.

lbl_appendix_name: Xcel Energy Minnesota — Large General Time of Day Service (25-289)

min_demand_threshold.detail: Very large customers are new loads of 100 MW or more, plus new 20-100 MW loads that are 'system intensive'.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: The Commission defined “very large customers” for purposes of Xcel’s tariffs as new loads sized 100 megawatts (MW) or greater.

min_contract_duration.verbatim: The Commission approved Xcel’s proposed 15-year default contract term and 24 month exit notice period.

min_bill.detail: Minimum bill set at 80% of contracted capacity, raised from Xcel's proposal.
min_bill.verbatim: the Commission increased the minimum bill and exit fee proposed by Xcel to 80% of the customer’s contracted capacity

min_billing_demand.detail: Minimum bill is tied to 80% of contracted capacity; the release does not describe it as a billing-demand floor.
min_billing_demand.verbatim: the Commission increased the minimum bill and exit fee proposed by Xcel to 80% of the customer’s contracted capacity

direct_cost_assignment.detail: All transmission and distribution upgrades needed to serve very large customers are paid by them as CIAC.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: All transmission and distribution upgrades needed to serve very large customers must be paid directly by those customers through Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC).

dca_interconnection.detail: Distribution upgrades needed to serve the customer are CIAC.
dca_interconnection.verbatim: All transmission and distribution upgrades needed to serve very large customers must be paid directly by those customers

dca_network_transmission.detail: Transmission upgrades needed to serve the customer are CIAC.
dca_network_transmission.verbatim: All transmission and distribution upgrades needed to serve very large customers must be paid directly by those customers

exit_fee.detail: Exit fee set at 80% of contracted capacity with a 24-month exit notice period.
exit_fee.verbatim: the Commission increased the minimum bill and exit fee proposed by Xcel to 80% of the customer’s contracted capacity

hold_harmless.detail: Xcel must file an Incremental Cost Test showing very large customers cover system, generation and transmission costs they create; Commission added OAG-recommended filing requirements.
hold_harmless.verbatim: The Commission approved Xcel’s Incremental Cost Test (ICT) but adopted new requirements recommended by the OAG

marginal_cost.detail: Incremental Cost Test compares costs of system, generation and transmission against revenue from the very large customer class.
marginal_cost.verbatim: ensure very large customers fully cover all of the system, generation, and transmission costs they create

customer_resource_procurement.detail: For each new customer Xcel must demonstrate supply meets Minnesota renewable and carbon-free benchmarks; a separate clean energy and capacity tariff is due Dec 1, 2026 (per ELPC).
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: For each new customer, Xcel must demonstrate that the electricity provided will meet Minnesota’s renewable and carbon free energy benchmarks

status_note: Approved: MN PUC decided at May 2026 meeting (news release May 18, 2026); written order dated June 12, 2026 ('Order Approving Tariffs, Creating the Very Large Customer Class', eDocket 20266-232841-01) per Oct 2026 XLI motion. The written order itself was not reachable; elements come from the PUC's own news release. Creates a standalone Very Large Customer class. Clean energy/capacity tariff due Dec 1, 2026 (ELPC).

lbl_appendix_name: NorthWestern Energy — Large New Load Tariff (2026.04.023)

min_demand_threshold.detail: Framework covers new or expanded customers with expected load of 5 MW or more; executed ESAs of 50 MW or more must be filed for PSC approval.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: onboarding new or expanded customers with an expected load of 5 megawatts or more

min_contract_duration.detail: Minimum service commitment periods, longer for loads of 50 MW or more; lengths not stated in the release.
min_contract_duration.verbatim: Minimum service commitment periods, including longer minimum terms for customers with very large loads (50 megawatts or greater)

min_billing_demand.detail: Minimum demand and minimum energy billing requirements in each ESA; percentages not stated in the release.
min_billing_demand.verbatim: Minimum demand and minimum energy billing requirements to ensure these customers pay for the capacity and energy needed to serve them

min_bill.detail: Minimum energy billing requirement in ESAs; amount not stated in the release.
min_bill.verbatim: Minimum demand and minimum energy billing requirements to ensure these customers pay for the capacity and energy needed to serve them

collateral.detail: Performance assurance and collateral requirements secure payment and performance; amounts set in the tariff/ESA.
collateral.verbatim: Performance assurance and collateral requirements to secure customer payment and performance obligations

exit_fee.detail: Termination cost provisions apply if a customer reduces load or terminates before the end of the term.
exit_fee.verbatim: Termination cost provisions designed to address costs remaining if a customer reduces load or terminates service before the end of the contract term

resize_reassign.detail: Termination costs also apply when a customer reduces load; reassignment is not described in the release.
resize_reassign.verbatim: costs remaining if a customer reduces load or terminates service before the end of the contract term

study_requirements.detail: Prospective customers sign a development agreement and fund studies of system impacts, infrastructure needs and feasibility before the ESA.
study_requirements.verbatim: prospective large new load customers first enter into a development agreement and fund studies to evaluate system impacts, infrastructure needs, and service feasibility

hold_harmless.detail: Stated purpose is that existing customers do not subsidize large new loads; no test or backstop is described in the release.
hold_harmless.verbatim: existing customers do not subsidize these large new load customers

status_note: Still proposed: filed April 1, 2026 at the Montana PSC; Earthjustice sought intervention and filed a July 9, 2026 motion on scope; no decision seen. Only the company's release and Daily Montanan were read; the filed tariff text (reservation charge, load factor, forecasting, collateral amounts) was not reached. Montana law requires a PSC finding of no adverse long-term impact for loads of 5 MW or more.

min_demand_threshold.detail: Applies to customers requesting at least 20 MW of electric demand (all large customers, not only data centers).
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: The tariff applies to customers requesting at least 20 megawatts of electric demand and meeting an 80 percent minimum load factor

load_factor_threshold.detail: Customers must meet an 80% minimum load factor.
load_factor_threshold.verbatim: meeting an 80 percent minimum load factor

min_contract_duration.detail: Customers commit to 15 years of energy service.
min_contract_duration.verbatim: commit to 15 years of energy service

min_bill.detail: Minimum monthly charge of at least 85% of the customer's contracted energy usage; no dollar figure is set.
min_bill.verbatim: the fees would be set at least 85% of the customer’s contracted energy usage

collateral.detail: Customers must provide a cash deposit; amount not stated.
collateral.verbatim: providing a cash deposit and covering the price of purchasing renewable energy

direct_cost_assignment.detail: Customers bear the costs and financial risks of serving their projects, including infrastructure and power supply.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: large-load customers will be responsible for the costs and financial risks associated with serving their projects, including needed infrastructure and power supply

dca_interconnection.detail: Customers cover substations and distribution facilities IID needs to serve them.
dca_interconnection.verbatim: including substations, distribution facilities and transmission lines

dca_network_transmission.detail: Customers cover transmission lines IID needs to deliver electricity to them.
dca_network_transmission.verbatim: including substations, distribution facilities and transmission lines

dca_generation_capacity.detail: Customer is responsible for power supply costs and for the price of renewable energy needed to meet state standards.
dca_generation_capacity.verbatim: covering the price of purchasing renewable energy to keep up with state environmental standards

study_requirements.detail: Formal process determines whether IID can reliably serve a proposed large load and what system improvements are required.
study_requirements.verbatim: The tariff also establishes a formal process for determining whether IID can reliably serve a proposed large load and what system improvements may be required.

customer_resource_procurement.detail: Tariff includes a curtailment-first provision for large users; no customer-procured resource option is described.
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: the pricing rules give IID the right to cut off power to those large users first

load_flexibility.detail: IID may curtail large-load customers first when demand surges; no compensation or program terms described.
load_flexibility.verbatim: the pricing rules give IID the right to cut off power to those large users first

status_note: Approved: IID Board voted unanimously Sept 15, 2026 (APPA, KESQ, KPBS). Tariff text not read; IID's own document not reached; details are from the APPA and KPBS reports of the board action.

min_demand_threshold.detail: Schedule 401 applies to Large Energy Use Facilities: data processing facilities using or able to use 20 MW or more.
min_demand_threshold.verbatim: a facility that uses or is able to use 20 megawatts or more and is primarily engaged in providing a service described under the 2022 North American Industry Classification System Code 518210

customer_type.detail: Schedule 401 is limited to facilities in NAICS 518210 (data processing, hosting and related services), per Oregon HB 3546.
customer_type.verbatim: “Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services.”

aggregation_rules.detail: Sites with common ownership within 2,500 feet or on the same substation count as one; data center customers with similar ownership statewide have contract demand summed.
aggregation_rules.verbatim: If two or more sites have common ownership and are within 2,500 feet of each other or are served by the same substation, the sites will be treated as one

min_contract_duration.detail: Minimum 10-year LEUF agreement term, up to 30 years including ramp; renewals at least 10 years.
min_contract_duration.verbatim: sets a minimum 10-year LEUF Agreement term, with a maximum term of 30 years, inclusive of any ramp period

load_ramp_period.detail: Ramp period is counted inside the 10 to 30 year term; no maximum ramp length set.
load_ramp_period.verbatim: sets a minimum 10-year LEUF Agreement term, with a maximum term of 30 years, inclusive of any ramp period

monthly_demand_charge.detail: Peak Demand Charge on the month's highest demand equal to the sum of OATT Schedule 1, Schedule 3 and network integration transmission service rates.
monthly_demand_charge.verbatim: will subject the New LEUF to a Peak Demand Charge that is based on the customer's highest demand during the month

collateral.detail: Customer must show A-/A3-level creditworthiness or post collateral covering its Exit Fee, reassessed every two years.
collateral.verbatim: a LEUF shall, at the company's election, be required to provide sufficient creditworthiness or post collateral to cover the customer's Exit Fee

direct_cost_assignment.detail: Direct contracting and direct assignment approach: network upgrades paid upfront, generation and storage costs recovered by reservation charge or customer resources.
direct_cost_assignment.verbatim: adopting a direct contracting and direct assignment approach

dca_interconnection.detail: Line extensions follow Rule 13; Network Upgrades needed to serve the facility are paid upfront by the customer.
dca_interconnection.verbatim: any Network Upgrades (as defined in Rule 13, including bulk transmission) required to serve the New LEUF's load will be paid for upfront by the New LEUF

dca_network_transmission.detail: Upfront payment of network upgrades, except qualified 230 kV+ WECC critical-path upgrades where the customer pays its usage share via monthly fee.
dca_network_transmission.verbatim: unless following criteria are all met: i. The Network Upgrade is a transmission facility of 230 kV and above

dca_generation_capacity.detail: Customer pays full cost of generation and storage resources via a monthly Reservation Charge on Contract Demand, or reimburses its own Customer Resources plus risk and firming charges.
dca_generation_capacity.verbatim: will require the New LEUF to compensate PacifiCorp for the full cost of all necessary generation and storage resources in one of two ways

customer_resource_procurement.detail: Option where the customer dictates the resources used to serve it ('Customer Resources').
customer_resource_procurement.verbatim: where the LEUF dictates the resources to be used to serve it (Customer Resources)

customer_led_procurement.detail: Customer Resources are reimbursed at actual cost plus a Portfolio Risk Management Charge and a System Firming and Balancing Charge (33% of system fixed generation).
customer_led_procurement.verbatim: a System Firming and Balancing Charge set at 33 percent of System Fixed Generation applicable to Schedule 48

load_flexibility.detail: Agreements may account for interruptible service; PacifiCorp must propose a flexibility compensation program in its next general rate case.
load_flexibility.verbatim: PacifiCorp will propose a uniform flexibility compensation program based on avoided cost principles for New LEUF customers

price_premium.detail: Community Energy Benefits Charge of 1 cent per kWh on facilities over 100 MW, funding energy efficiency, home repairs or DER for low-income customers (reverts to 0 if the PGE charge is struck down).
price_premium.verbatim: imposes a 1 cent/kW charge on LEUFs over 100 MW to fund non-cost-effective energy efficiency, critical home repairs

study_requirements.detail: $25,000 non-refundable application fee; engineering studies funded by and allocated fully to the customer; study cost true-up.
study_requirements.verbatim: imposes a $25,000 nonrefundable application fee as an offset to the costs of PacifiCorp's preparing the LEUF Agreement

hold_harmless.detail: Schedule must mitigate unwarranted cost shifting; each agreement must not harm resource adequacy or HB 2021 compliance for existing customers.
hold_harmless.verbatim: Each LEUF Agreement will ensure that the New LEUF's load is served in a manner that does not harm PacifiCorp's resource adequacy position

no_harm_analysis.detail: PacifiCorp must analyze the generation and capacity resources needed to serve each new LEUF without impeding HB 2021 compliance, filed with each agreement approval.
no_harm_analysis.verbatim: requires that each standard LEUF Agreement and Schedule 401 require PacifiCorp to analyze the generation and capacity resources necessary to serve the New LEUF's load

exit_fee.detail: Exit fee covers net book value of company-funded infrastructure, customer-specific power agreements, remaining Reservation Charge and removal costs.
exit_fee.verbatim: The Exit Fee will include the net book value of company-funded infrastructure

resize_reassign.detail: Exit fee is refunded pro rata if another large customer takes the capacity within three years.
resize_reassign.verbatim: If another large customer takes service within three years of an exiting LEUF's departure, the Exit Fee will be refunded by a pro-rata share of the capacity assumed by the new large customer.

status_note: Now approved: Oregon PUC Order No. 26-443, entered Nov 13, 2026, adopts the Sept 16, 2026 stipulation (Docket UE 463; suspension had run to Dec 31, 2026). Seed record says approved; LBL (Aug 2026) listed it as pending. Read the order text directly.
